title: Saâdane Afif: Five Preludes
description: The focus of Saâdane Afif’s exhibition at Hamburger Bahnhof is his multi-piece work, The Fountain Archives, which was given to the Nationalgalerie in 2023 and is being presented to the public for the first time at Hamburger Bahnhof.

title: Giulia Andreani: Sabotage
description: In February 2026, painter Giulia Andreani opens the exhibition programme marking the 30th anniversary of Hamburger Bahnhof, presenting paintings that expose fractures within official histories.

title: Seeing Words, Reading Images – The Written Art Collection in dialogue with the Deutsche Bank Collection
description: The exhibition focuses on the contemporary perspective, a kind of worldwide written art that centers on the global dialogue of today's artistic positions.

title: Shilpa Gupta: What Still Holds
description: Starting point of Shilpa Gupta’s solo exhibition at Hamburger Bahnhof is the monumental work Truth, situated at the intersection of language, power, and control.

title: Marina Abramović: Balkan Erotic Epic
description: Marina Abramović's exhibition at Berlin's Gropis Bau focuses on her ongoing interest in rituals, eroticism, death, and the body as a site of political resistance.

title: Marc Brandenburg: 20th Century Debris
description: The exhibition at the Berlinische Galerie is dedicated to the multifaceted work of Marc Brandenburg, who has been shaping the Berlin art scene for decades.

title: New Woman, New Vision: Women Photographers of the Bauhaus
venue: Museum für Fotografie - Helmut Newton Stiftung
description: The female photographers at the Bauhaus experimented with photographic and design techniques, exploring the limits of their medium.

title: Intermezzo: Revisiting Helmut Newton
venue: Museum für Fotografie - Helmut Newton Stiftung
description: The new permanent exhibition at the Museum of Photography will respond even more dynamically to the different aspects of Helmut and June Newton's photographic works.

title: Ruin and Rush: Berlin 1910–1930
description: With the exhibition Ruin and Rush, the Neue Nationalgalerie focuses on selected works from its collection of Classical Modernism that address the Berlin of the 1910s and 1920s.

title: Fujiko Nakaya: Fog Sculpture in the Sculpture Garden
description: Due to the great public interest, the NeueNationalgalerie will once again present the site-specific fog sculpture byJapanese artist Fujiko Nakaya in its sculpture garden in 2026.

title: Lina Lapelytė: We Make Years Out of Hours – Chanel Commission
description: For the second edition of the Chanel Commission Lina Lapelytė will transform the Historic Hall into a polyphonic stage for a participatory choreography.

title: Anton Corbijn: Corbijn, Anton
description: The portraits by photographer Anton Corbijn, who has been accompanying influential artists on the international music and culture scene for decades, are known worldwide.

title: Rooftop Screening: City Fragments
description: Manually curated screening added as a fallback example without prefilled coordinates.

title: Many Shades of Grès: Fashion Becomes Art
description: French fashion designer Madame Grès was considered one of the most important pioneers of haute couture in the 20th century.

title: Cassirer and the Breakthrough of Impressionism
description: In 2026, the Alte Nationalgalerie is paying tribute to Paul Cassirer (1871-1926), one of the most important art dealers of his time.

title: Rooms / Stages
venue: Museum für Fotografie - Helmut Newton Stiftung
description: The exhibition “Rooms / Stages” dispenses with artistic documentation, instead shifting the context and focus from the performative act to the stage space itself.

title: Kyiv Biennial: A Bird That Cannot Land
description: The Kyiv Biennial in Berlin is a nomadic, international project that interweaves artistic, political, and social issues.

title: Gabriele Stötzer: Dabei sein und nicht schweigen
description: For over five decades, Gabriele Stötzer has been addressing issues such as justice, self-determination, and gender.

title: Walter Schels: 16° Pisces – Retrospective
description: In celebration of Walter Schels’s ninetieth birthday, C/O Berlin and the F.C. Gundlach Foundation present the photographer’s first retrospective in Berlin.

title: Materialistin: Matter of Care, Care of Matter
description: The exhibition features sculptures and site-specific installations at the Hamburger Bahnhof that explore social and cultural-political issues.

title: Paul Signac: Symphony of Colors
description: Achieving the highest degree of luminosity and harmony—this was the goal Paul Signac set himself when he introduced a new style of painting to the art world in the mid-1880s together with Georges Seurat.

title: Iván Argote: A Place To Stay
description: Through his sculptures, installations, films, and interventions, Iván Argote consistently explores the relationships between people, power structures, and belief systems, and challenges prevailing historical narratives.

title: Bjørn Melhus: Lost in Finity
description: The starting point is newly curated material drawn from Bjørn Melhus’s 35 years of artistic practice, which resonates with the present in an uncanny way: religious imagery meets pop-cultural visions of the apocalypse and technoid exit strategies.

title: Everybody
description: The artworks on display focus on the body not as a static category, but as a dynamic construct shaped by social, historical, and emotional influences.
